D006-D005_h001.question:
"I'm really struggling, doctor. It's been about ten months since things really took a turn. I'd be flying high, feeling like I could sell every house in the county, talking a mile a minute, bouncing between calls, drawing up contracts, reorganizing the files, then suddenly wanting to redecorate my entire house – 'decorate, ornate, make it great,' I'd think. But then my mood would just crash, and I'd feel nothing, just an emptiness where joy used to be. Sometimes I get these awful thoughts, fleeting urges to just… step into traffic, even though I know I shouldn't.

But the really scary stuff started about eight months ago, while all this manic energy and crushing sadness was still going on. I started seeing things, like shimmering figures at the edge of my vision, people waving at me from empty parking lots. And the TV… it feels like the newscasters are sending me coded messages, just for me, through their expressions. I know it sounds crazy, but it feels so real.

What's really been rough is that these strange visions and those secret messages, they're not just happening when I'm feeling intensely high or low. For the past couple of weeks, I’ve been feeling relatively stable mood-wise, not those extreme ups and downs, but those visual hallucinations and that feeling of being communicated with directly have still been there, lingering even without the mood swings. It’s definitely been longer than a few weeks that I've been dealing with the mania predominantly, it's just that these other things have been constant too, regardless of how high or low my mood was at the time."
D006-D005_h001.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D006-D005_h002.question:
It’s hard to even describe what’s been going on, doc. For the better part of a year now, ten months actually, it feels like I’m constantly buzzing. My wife, she says I don’t sit still for a second. I try to get things done, but then my mind just flits from one thing to another, never really settling. One minute I'm on top of the world, feeling like I can solve every case, and the next I want to smash something. My squad car feels too small, my uniform too tight.

And then, things started getting really weird about eight months ago. I’d be on patrol, and it felt like bugs were crawling on my skin, or someone was messing with my hair. I’d swat at nothing, and the guys would look at me funny. Sometimes when I try to explain it, the words just… they don’t come out right. It’s like my thoughts get all jumbled and then what I say is just a mess, a word salad. It's like I know what I want to say about the world ending, about a great flood coming, but then I hear the whispers and the buzzing and I just lose it.

In the midst of all this, I went through a really dark patch, about three months ago. I just couldn’t bring myself to do anything. Getting out of bed felt impossible, and I just wanted it all to stop. I… I tried to end it then. And what’s really odd, is that even when I was at my absolute lowest, convinced the world was collapsing in on itself, those crawling sensations, those mixed-up words, they were still there, clear as day, for at least a couple of weeks, even without the intense mood swings. But these periods where my mood is just wild, cycling from high to low and back again, that restlessness, that’s actually been the majority of the time I’ve been feeling off.
D006-D005_h002.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D006-D005_h003.question:
"Honestly, doc, I don't even know where to start. Things have been... out of whack for a while now. For about ten months, I've had this buzzing under my skin, like I've chugged a dozen energy drinks. I can't sit still, always got to be doing something. My wife, she says I'm like a tornado. I'll start tearing apart an engine, then suddenly I'm cleaning out the garage, then I'm sketching some wild new invention for a flying car. Nothing ever gets finished. My mood's a rollercoaster too – one minute I'm on top of the world, feeling like I'm destined for greatness, the next I'm snapping at my wife for no reason.

And that's not even the strangest part. For the past eight months, things have gotten really weird. I've been seeing people in the shop that aren't there, just walking around, pointing at me. And my thoughts... sometimes it’s like my brain is trying to speak a language I don't understand, just a jumble of words that don't make sense. It’s hard to carry on a conversation when my tongue feels all tangled up. These strange visions and mixed-up thoughts have been happening pretty much alongside all that high energy and mood stuff.

But then, sometimes even when I’m feeling totally myself, not super high or down, those visuals still pop up. There was a stretch of about three weeks, maybe a month, not that long ago, where I was just feeling normal, not manic, not depressed, but I was still seeing shadows moving in my peripheral vision and hearing faint whispers, even when I knew nobody else was around. Then, for the last three months, it's been the complete opposite. I just can't bring myself to do anything. Even getting out of bed feels like climbing Mount Everest. I tried to just give up a few weeks ago, took a bunch of pills… didn’t work, obviously. I just can't keep living like this."
D006-D005_h003.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D006-D005_h004.question:

I can't sit still, constantly moving, jumping from one thing to another. The problem is, this wired, high-energy feeling has been pretty much constant throughout all of this, even when those strange thoughts and voices are at their worst.

And then, about three months ago, it all just crashed. I completely withdrew, didn't want to see anyone, barely got out of bed. It got so bad that I started thinking about ways to end it all, really specific plans about how I'd do it. It’s just so exhausting.

    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D006-D005_h005.question:
It's been almost a year now, and I’m just so exhausted. I used to love my work at the museum, curating exhibits, but lately, everything feels flat, just… pointless. I can't focus on anything; my mind is scattered, flitting from one thought to another. It's like my brain won't settle.

About ten months ago, I started feeling this incredible energy, buzzing, like I could conquer the world. I’d try to work on a new exhibit, get all these grand ideas, but then I'd be up for days without sleep, pacing my apartment, feeling restless, needing to *do* something, anything! It's been like this for most of the past year – waves of this intense high, where I’m incredibly irritable and restless, followed by awful lows.

But it’s also been about eight months since I started smelling things that aren't there – foul, metallic smells, sometimes even burning plastic – even when I'm alone in my apartment. And I started believing the world was ending, that some catastrophic event was just around the corner. These bizarre smells and terrifying thoughts about the world ending haven't gone away, even during the periods when I fall into a deep depression, losing all interest in life, sometimes just wishing I could disappear. There have been times, sometimes for weeks, when I have these strange smells and these intense, scary convictions about impending doom, even when my mood isn’t swinging wildly up or down.
D006-D005_h005.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D006-D005_h006.question:

The worst part is, these delusions and smells have been happening for weeks at a time even when I’m not feeling this intense high. D006-D005_h008.question:

I'll be working on one schematic, then suddenly I'm sketching out a completely different concept, then I'm writing down some "insights" I've had. My mind just races, jumping from one idea to the next, and I can't seem to finish anything. It's incredibly frustrating because I know I'm capable, but I'm just always on edge, short-tempered with my colleagues, and find myself pacing the lab when I should be sitting still. But then there are these other things... I keep getting these uncomfortable crawling sensations on my skin, like tiny insects under the surface, which is incredibly distracting. And I can't shake the feeling that my landlord, who usually doesn't care, is leaving the hallway light off at specific times meaning something to me. This whole state, the agitation and the strange sensations, they've been pretty constant together for well over a year and a half now, almost the entire time I've been feeling off. What's worse is that even when I'm feeling alright emotionally, not ramped up, those weird feelings and the strange meanings I see in things still crop up. Just a few weeks ago, for two whole weeks, I was mostly just dealing with the bugs under my skin and thinking the news headlines were secretly about me, even when my mood was pretty stable.
D006-D005_h008.options:

D006-D005_h009.question:

My mind races, jumping from one idea to the next, designing new pieces at a furious pace. Every little noise outside, every car passing by, it pulls my attention, like there's always something more important to see. For most of these past two years, more often than not, I've been feeling this surge of energy and elevated mood, even when I'm seeing and feeling these other things. There have been a few weeks here and there, though, where the visions and the feeling of being watched were still very much there, but that intense, unstoppable energy wasn't around at all. I was just... me, with the strange things happening. But mostly, it's been both.
D006-D005_h009.options:

    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

D006-D005_h010.question:

D006-D005_h011.question:

Even when I’m not in one of those high-energy moods, those crawling sensations and the feeling of being watched are still there. Just a few months ago, for about two weeks, I was feeling good, no crazy highs or lows, but those feelings of bugs on my skin and the belief that competitors were monitoring me were still very present. Then came the lows. For five months, I've just felt this deep, heavy sadness, and this crushing guilt, like every failure, big or small, is entirely my fault and I deserve whatever bad happens.
